description: Two-seat Lightning T.55K, one of two delivered to Kuwait 1969. Preserved inside the Kuwait Air Force Museum hangars at Al Mubarak / Nawaf Al-Ahmad Air Base (Flickr 'Aircraft throughout the years' 2016; Thunder & Lightnings survivors list 'Air Museum, Kuwait International Airport'; Scramble; aviagraphers.net visit Jan 2018). aviationmuseum.eu prints the serial as '53-411/B', a typo. Museum is on the military side and not open to the public; opened to visitors during the Kuwait Aviation Show (Jan 2018, Jan 2020).
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base

description: Jet Provost T.51 KAF101, c/n 10-23 per JetPhotos (Sebastian Sowa, 16 Jan 2020, 'preserved at the Kuwait Air Force Museum on the military premises at Kuwait International Airport'). Also listed by aviationmuseum.eu and aviagraphers.net (2018).
aliases: Jet Provost T51; KAF101; JP T.51
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base

description: Hunter F.57 listed by aviationmuseum.eu as '214/D' and by aviagraphers.net (Jan 2018 visit) as 'Hunter F.Mk.57 serial 214' in the Kuwait Air Force Museum hangar. A second Hunter (see 213) stands at the base gate. Thunder & Lightnings lists two unidentified F.57s at Kuwait International Airport, one on display and one dumped; the identity 214 rests on the two museum visit reports.
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base

description: A-4KU BuNo 160184. Captured by Iraq in August 1990 (dstorm.eu: 'POW, damaged in Iraq, now in museum at Kuwait IAP'); photographed preserved at Kuwait International (military side) in March 1994 (ABPic, Rico Swytech) and listed in the museum by aviationmuseum.eu and aviagraphers.net (2018). Wears 'Free Kuwait' Gulf War markings per tristaraviation.org. A-4KU 821 (BuNo 160200) exists as dumped wreckage with the museum (Flickr 2016) and is not recorded as a display.
aliases: A4KU; 160184; Skyhawk A-4KU; A-4 Skyhawk; A4
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base

description: Two-seat TA-4KU BuNo 160210. Captured by Iraq 1990, damaged, now in the museum (dstorm.eu). Photographed March 1994 (ABPic, c/n 14578) and 2016 (Flickr 'Aircraft throughout the years': 'preserved with Kuwait Air Force museum, Al Mubarak / Nawaf Ahmad Air Base'). First of two TA-4KUs at the museum.
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base

description: Two-seat TA-4KU BuNo 160211, c/n 14579. Disassembled and trucked to Iraq in 1990, recovered, now in the museum (dstorm.eu). Photographed March 1994 (ABPic), October 2016 (Flickr) and 16 Jan 2020 'preserved in front of the Kuwait Air Force Museum' (JetPhotos, Sebastian Sowa). Displayed outside the museum hangar in desert camouflage with 'Free Kuwait' titles. Second of two TA-4KUs at the museum.
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base

description: Mirage F1CK 715, preserved with the KAF museum at Al Mubarak / Nawaf Al-Ahmad Air Base (Flickr 2016; aviationmuseum.eu; aviagraphers.net Jan 2018, which notes it lacks its canopy).
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base

description: Auster J/5F Aiglet Trainer, former Kuwait civil registration 9K-AAD, representing the Austers with which the Kuwait Air Force was formed in 1953-54. In the museum hangar (aviationmuseum.eu; aviagraphers.net 2018). Painted markings not confirmed.
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base

description: Westland WS-55 Whirlwind Series 1, c/n WA.319 (aviagraphers.net, which calls it the sole survivor of its type in the collection). aviationmuseum.eu lists it as '313 Westland WS-55 Srs.1'; the serial 313 is taken from that listing and is unverified. Inside the museum hangar.
museum_name: Kuwait Air Force Museum, Abdullah Al-Mubarak Air Base
